title: Maximum Number of Coins You Can Get
summary: Given an array of pile sizes, players take turns picking piles in a specific order: Alice picks the largest, then you pick the next largest, and Bob takes the remaining pile.
statement: Given an array of pile sizes, players take turns picking piles in a specific order: Alice picks the largest, then you pick the next largest, and Bob takes the remaining pile. Repeat until all piles are taken. Return the maximum number of coins you can collect.
constraints: The number of piles is a multiple of three; from each chosen triple Alice takes the largest, you take the next largest, and Bob takes the remaining pile.
Rearrange triples to maximize your total.
hints: For each round, discard the current largest pile to Alice, take the next largest, and reserve the globally smallest piles for Bob.
Repeat for one third of the pile count.
Any larger pile given to Bob can be exchanged with a smaller unused pile without hurting Alice’s dominance and only improving your options.
editorial: Any larger pile given to Bob can be exchanged with a smaller unused pile without hurting Alice’s dominance and only improving your options.

tests.explanation: Pairing the largest piles lets you take seven and two, totaling nine.
Alice takes five, you take four, and Bob takes two.
